verses.text: And the LORD said to Job:

xrefs.text: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:
Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:

verses.text: “Will the faultfinder contend with the Almighty? Let him who argues with God give an answer.”

xrefs.text: “For who has known the mind of the Lord, so as to instruct Him?” But we have the mind of Christ.
Whom did He consult to enlighten Him, and who taught Him the paths of justice? Who imparted knowledge to Him and showed Him the way of understanding?
“Who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been His counselor?”
Why do you complain to Him that He answers nothing a man asks?
The One who vindicates Me is near. Who will dare to contend with Me? Let us confront each other! Who has a case against Me? Let him approach Me!

verses.text: Then Job answered the LORD:
“Behold, I am insignificant. How can I reply to You? I place my hand over my mouth.

xrefs.text: If you have foolishly exalted yourself or if you have plotted evil, put your hand over your mouth.
The princes refrained from speaking and covered their mouths with their hands.
Look at me and be appalled; put your hand over your mouth.
Therefore I despise myself, and I repent in dust and ashes.”

“Be quiet,” they told him. “Put your hand over your mouth and come with us and be a father and a priest to us. Is it better for you to be a priest for the house of one person or a priest for a tribe and family in Israel?”

verses.text: I have spoken once, but I have no answer— twice, but I have nothing to add.”

xrefs.text: For God speaks in one way and in another, yet no one notices.
God has spoken once; I have heard this twice: that power belongs to God,
If one wished to contend with God, he could not answer Him one time out of a thousand.
For even if I were right, I could not answer. I could only beg my Judge for mercy.
Suppose someone says to God, ‘I have endured my punishment; I will offend no more.

verses.text: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:

xrefs.text: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:
But the Day of the Lord will come like a thief. The heavens will disappear with a roar, the elements will be destroyed by fire, and the earth and its works will be laid bare.
Our God approaches and will not be silent! Consuming fire precedes Him, and a tempest rages around Him.
For you have not come to a mountain that can be touched and that is burning with fire; to darkness, gloom, and storm;

verses.text: “Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me.

xrefs.text: Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me.
You said, ‘Listen now, and I will speak. I will question you, and you shall inform Me.’
If only I knew where to find Him, so that I could go to His seat.
Then call me, and I will answer, or let me speak, and You can reply.

verses.text: Would you really annul My justice? Would you condemn Me to justify yourself?

xrefs.text: Certainly not! Let God be true and every man a liar. As it is written: “So that You may be proved right when You speak and victorious when You judge.”
This kindled the anger of Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram. He burned with anger against Job for justifying himself rather than God,
Your covenant with death will be dissolved, and your agreement with Sheol will not stand. When the overwhelming scourge passes through, you will be trampled by it.
For Job has declared, ‘I am righteous, yet God has deprived me of justice.
The LORD of Hosts has purposed, and who can thwart Him? His hand is outstretched, so who can turn it back?

verses.text: Do you have an arm like God’s? Can you thunder with a voice like His?

xrefs.text: Then there comes a roaring sound; He thunders with His majestic voice. He does not restrain the lightning when His voice resounds.
Woe to him who quarrels with his Maker— one clay pot among many. Does the clay ask the potter, ‘What are you making?’ Does your work say, ‘He has no hands’?
Mighty is Your arm; strong is Your hand. Your right hand is exalted.
My heart grew hot within me; as I mused, the fire burned. Then I spoke with my tongue:
God is wise in heart and mighty in strength. Who has resisted Him and prospered?

verses.text: Then adorn yourself with majesty and splendor, and clothe yourself with honor and glory.

xrefs.text: The LORD reigns! He is robed in majesty; the LORD has clothed and armed Himself with strength. The world indeed is firmly established; it cannot be moved.
For the LORD takes pleasure in His people; He adorns the afflicted with salvation.
He put on righteousness like a breastplate, and the helmet of salvation on His head; He put on garments of vengeance and wrapped Himself in a cloak of zeal.

Yours, O LORD, is the greatness and the power and the glory and the splendor and the majesty, for everything in heaven and on earth belongs to You. Yours, O LORD, is the kingdom, and You are exalted as head over all.
Bless the LORD, O my soul! O LORD my God, You are very great; You are clothed with splendor and majesty.

verses.text: Unleash the fury of your wrath; look on every proud man and bring him low.

xrefs.text: Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and exalt and glorify the King of heaven, for all His works are true and all His ways are just. And He is able to humble those who walk in pride.
So the pride of man will be brought low, and the loftiness of men will be humbled; the LORD alone will be exalted in that day,
The proud look of man will be humbled, and the loftiness of men brought low; the LORD alone will be exalted in that day.
Who can withstand His indignation? Who can endure His burning anger? His wrath is poured out like fire; even rocks are shattered before Him.
Now I know that the LORD is greater than all other gods, for He did this when they treated Israel with arrogance.”

verses.text: Look on every proud man and humble him; trample the wicked where they stand.

xrefs.text: “I have trodden the winepress alone, and no one from the nations was with Me. I trampled them in My anger and trod them down in My fury; their blood spattered My garments, and all My clothes were stained.
Then you will trample the wicked, for they will be ashes under the soles of your feet on the day I am preparing,” says the LORD of Hosts.
With God we will perform with valor, and He will trample our enemies.
I will punish the world for its evil and the wicked for their iniquity. I will end the haughtiness of the arrogant and lay low the pride of the ruthless.
The LORD sends poverty and wealth; He humbles and He exalts.

verses.text: Bury them together in the dust; imprison them in the grave.

xrefs.text: Go into the rocks and hide in the dust from the terror of the LORD and the splendor of His majesty.
Like sheep they are destined for Sheol. Death will be their shepherd. The upright will rule them in the morning, and their form will decay in Sheol, far from their lofty abode.
The godless in heart harbor resentment; even when He binds them, they do not cry for help.
If only You would hide me in Sheol and conceal me until Your anger has passed! If only You would appoint a time for me and then remember me!

Just as the king returned from the palace garden to the banquet hall, Haman was falling on the couch where Esther was reclining. The king exclaimed, “Would he actually assault the queen while I am in the palace?” As soon as the words had left the king’s mouth, they covered Haman’s face.

verses.text: Then I will confess to you that your own right hand can save you.

xrefs.text: For at just the right time, while we were still powerless, Christ died for the ungodly.
For it was not by their sword that they took the land; their arm did not bring them victory. It was by Your right hand, Your arm, and the light of Your face, because You favored them.
But because of His great love for us, God, who is rich in mercy,
He gives power to the faint and increases the strength of the weak.
For I do not trust in my bow, nor does my sword save me.

verses.text: Look at Behemoth, which I made along with you. He feeds on grass like an ox.

xrefs.text: The hills yield him their produce, while all the beasts of the field play nearby.
And God said, “Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds: livestock, land crawlers, and beasts of the earth according to their kinds.” And it was so.
He makes the grass grow for the livestock and provides crops for man to cultivate, bringing forth food from the earth:
He roams the mountains for pasture, searching for any green thing.

verses.text: See the strength of his loins and the power in the muscles of his belly.
His tail sways like a cedar; the sinews of his thighs are tightly knit.

xrefs.text: The folds of his flesh are tightly joined; they are firm and immovable.

verses.text: His bones are tubes of bronze; his limbs are rods of iron.

xrefs.text: For I knew that you are stubborn; your neck is iron and your forehead is bronze.
Am I the sea, or the monster of the deep, that You must keep me under guard?

verses.text: He is the foremost of God’s works; only his Maker can draw the sword against him.

xrefs.text: Nothing on earth is his equal— a creature devoid of fear!
In that day the LORD will take His sharp, great, and mighty sword, and bring judgment on Leviathan the fleeing serpent Leviathan the coiling serpent— and He will slay the dragon of the sea.
How many are Your works, O LORD! In wisdom You have made them all; the earth is full of Your creatures.
By His breath the skies were cleared; His hand pierced the fleeing serpent.
If one does not repent, God will sharpen His sword; He has bent and strung His bow.

verses.text: He lies under the lotus plants, hidden among the reeds of the marsh.

xrefs.text: The parched ground will become a pool, the thirsty land springs of water. In the haunt where jackals once lay, there will be grass and reeds and papyrus.
The canals will stink; the streams of Egypt will trickle and dry up; the reeds and rushes will wither.

verses.text: The lotus plants conceal him in their shade; the willows of the brook surround him.

xrefs.text: He took some of the seed of the land and planted it in fertile soil; he placed it by abundant waters and set it out like a willow.
So they carry their wealth and belongings over the Brook of the Willows.

On the first day you are to gather the fruit of majestic trees, the branches of palm trees, and the boughs of leafy trees and of willows of the brook. And you are to rejoice before the LORD your God for seven days.

verses.text: Though the river rages, Behemoth is unafraid; he remains secure, though the Jordan surges to his mouth.
